content.text:
I submitted index 3 (Cr 0.29, Fe 0.48, V 0.23) as the best composition. Its photocurrent was 2.3e-7 A, the highest of the three I measured.

The merit budget was only 3 measurements across 201 compositions, so I tested one spot in each of three regions:

| Index | Cr / Fe / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 29 | 0.23 / 0.37 / 0.39 | 2.2e-7 |
| 22 | 0.20 / 0.14 / 0.66 | 3e-8 |
| 3 | 0.29 / 0.48 / 0.23 | 2.3e-7 |

- **Index 29** was my first guess, based on prior knowledge rather than data: roughly equal Fe and V with some Cr added, on the idea that iron vanadate (FeVO₄) is a known photoanode material.
- **Index 22**, a vanadium-rich composition, was about 7× worse.
- **Index 3**, with more Fe and less V, came out slightly above index 29.

Index 3 only beats index 29 by a small margin, so compositions in that area look about the same so far. With three points I can't tell whether the true best is near index 3 or somewhere unmeasured, such as the chromium-rich or even more iron-rich parts of the library. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements or the phase database, so I have no crystal-structure evidence for why index 3 does better.
